text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - British stocks ended firmer Monday as momentum from the FTSE's dramatic rise Friday continued amid subsiding fears of an inflationary budget Tuesday, and after Wall Street stocks reached their latest record peak. The FTSE 100 index of leading shares added another 35.9 points to finish at 4,054.6, within reach of its all-time record of 4,073.2 set Oct. 21.
FRANKFURT - German shares climbed to new record highs Monday, boosted by strength in the dollar, which benefits German exporters, and gains in market newcomer Deutsche Telekom.
The German DAX index of 30 top shares ended floor trade at a record market level of 2,799.19 points, up 35.50 points. In after-hours trade, the index rose 31.05 to 2,800.52.

PARIS - French stocks, buoyed by bulls, headed higher Monday to put on nearly another 1 percent after Friday's climb of 0.98 percent. "It's bulls all the way," one broker said. Paris is one of the markets which has not regained its all-time high and the CAC index has potential to hit 2,300 in the next few weeks, the second broker added.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 21.67 points at 2,277.14.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended slightly firmer in slack trade Monday after profit taking erased most early gains.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) slipped below the technically and psychologically important level of 3,900 points after posting an intraday record high of 3,906.2 points.

Volumes were described as low. "It was a typical Monday bourse," a dealer said. Investors were cautious given the record levels on Wall Street. "But even if there is a correction in New York, it will probably not mar good sentiment here," he aded. The all-share SPI firmed 3.81 points to 2,485.40.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks finished the Monday session with moderate gains, mainly from blue-chip shares, brokers said. They added, however, that the key Nikkei benchmark was still in a boxed range and likely to remain so until a key business sentiment survey comes out later this week. At the end of the day, the Nikkei 225 was up 77.46 points at 21,293.57.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index scored a record close Monday, taking its cue from Wall Street's shattering of more records Friday and buoyed by continued bullish sentiment in the property market. The index closed 122.60 points higher at 13,239.39 after setting a record intraday high at 13,261.25.

SYDNEY - Australian shares finished at a record close Monday after rising modestly from the open following the continued strength of the Dow, which achieved another record high close Friday. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 11.3 points higher at 2,394.7, two points higher than its previous record close of 2,392.7, set Thursday.
JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares dived on a weak bullion price, which fixed in London at its lowest level in 20 months, shaving over 2 percent off the index.
Industrial shares retraced earlier losses ending a touch firmer, boosted by futures players in afternoon trade.

But dealers said trade was hampered for most of the day by the Johannesburg Equities Trading system, which was initially shut down for three hours in the morning and again at 8:10 a.m. EST for the rest of the trading session following response problems.
The market was seen continuing volatile Tuesday on a weak bullion price and fears of a correction on Wall Street.
The gold index ended down 39.2 points at 1,621.3 points, pulling the all-share index down 35.4 points to 6,691.3. The industrial index was up 2.8 points at 7,954.8 points.
